sections.h2: Who sends and collects the bill
sections.html:
The elected Tax Commissioner does both jobs. The office mails roughly 28,000 property tax bills a year and collects the county, county Board of Education and state property taxes. It also takes exemption applications, issues executions against delinquent taxpayers and sells vehicle tags.

Walk-in service is on the ground level of Government Plaza at 215 North Wall Street, Calhoun, GA 30701. Call 706-629-9242 on weekdays between 8:30 am and 5 pm. Mailed payments go to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703. Enclose a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Gordon County
sections.html:
Gordon County has 61,701 residents, up 7.2 percent since 2020. Of its 24,859 housing units, owners occupy 73.9 percent, and the median value of an owned home is $222,900. Median household income is $63,650, and 289 building permits were pulled in 2025.

Interstate 75 runs through the middle of the county, so commute distance matters to buyers. Manufacturing is the main source of local jobs. Cities are Calhoun, Fairmount and Plainville, and Resaca is a town.

sections.h2: When Gordon County property tax bills are due
sections.html:
The state default is December 20, but a county can pick a different date, so trust the one on your own bill. For 2026 the county mailed bills before October 31 and set the due date on or before December 31. The county also set a lower rate for 2026.

Online payment goes through the county's tax payment site, which asks you to accept a disclaimer first. A credit card payment carries a 2.50 percent convenience fee charged by the processor, not by the county. Mail a check to the post office box above to skip it. For delinquent bills more than seven years old, contact the tax commissioner's office directly.

  • Card payment online: 2.50 percent convenience fee, set by the processor.
  • Check by mail: P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703, no fee.
  • Questions on older years: the tax commissioner's office, by phone or in person.

A property may be under appeal even when the website does not show it. Call 706-629-9242 for the most accurate balance before closing, and get the payoff in writing for your closing agent. Staff can tell you whether a parcel has more than one year outstanding.

Your yearly assessment notice spells out how to appeal. A challenge to market value goes by mail to the assessors' board, and the envelope needs a postmark inside the 45 days that follow the notice's mailing. With about 28,000 bills going out, comparing your value with neighbors' is worth the time.

  • Keep the notice envelope, because the mailing date starts the clock.
  • Gather recent sales of similar houses and any contractor repair estimates.
  • Ask the assessors' office which forms and evidence it prefers.
  • Ask the tax commissioner how an appealed parcel appears on the bill before you pay.

In Gordon County the tax commissioner takes exemption applications. File once the house becomes your primary residence; April 1 closes the first year you want the benefit, and a skipped application counts as a waiver. The return window runs January 1 through April 1. Skip it after returning or paying last year, and the county treats the property as filed at last year's final value.

Vehicle and mobile home paperwork also runs through this office, which issues county and city mobile home decals and transfers vehicle titles. If you are moving a mobile home off the lot, ask what must be settled first.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you list
sections.html:
A short checklist saves trouble at the closing table.

  1. Call the Tax Commissioner at 706-629-9242 and ask whether the parcel has any year outstanding, not just the current one.
  2. Ask for the payoff figure in writing and keep a copy for your closing attorney.
  3. Check the assessment notice for your parcel and note the date it was mailed, in case a challenge is still open.
  4. Confirm that your homestead exemption is on file, and tell the office when you move so the next owner can apply.
  5. If the property includes a mobile home, ask whether the home and the land sit on separate accounts and which decal paperwork must be finished first.

None of this requires a lawyer, though your closing attorney will want the paperwork in hand before the contract date. A buyer's lender will order a title search that picks up any execution, so a clean record means fewer surprises late in the process.

A city can levy a separate tax and bill it through the city clerk, unless the city and county agreed on one combined bill. If you live in Calhoun, Fairmount, Plainville or Resaca, find out how many bills to expect.

Calhoun also runs its own city school system, so a home inside city limits may sit in a different district than one served by the county system. Ask the tax commissioner which school levy applies to your parcel before you quote a monthly cost to a buyer.

Unpaid balances can pick up interest after the 60 days that follow a bill's postmark, and penalties may be added on top. The tax commissioner issues executions against delinquent taxpayers, and a recorded execution stays on the title until it is paid. If tax was wrongly assessed or collected, you have three years from the payment to ask for a refund.

If you owe, ask for the payoff in writing, hand it to the closing attorney, and expect the title company to settle it from the sale money. We buy Gordon County houses as-is for cash, including homes in Calhoun and the smaller towns along I-75 where an owner has older repairs, tenants or back taxes. A cash buyer still needs a clear title, so the payoff is handled the same way.

If an heir received the house under a recorded beneficiary deed, our Georgia transfer on death page lists what must be recorded before a sale.

A cash buyer does not wait on a lender's appraisal or underwriting, so the closing date depends mostly on title work and the tax payoff. That suits an owner who must move soon or who inherited a house with unpaid years. The payoff still comes from your proceeds, which is why the written figure from the Tax Commissioner matters even when no bank is involved.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Gordon County property tax?
faqs.a: Use the county's online payment site, or mail a check to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703. The office is at 215 North Wall Street in Calhoun and takes calls at 706-629-9242.

faqs.q: How much did Gordon County lower its tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The 2026 rate is 7.7 mills, down from 9.042 mills in 2024 and 2025. The last lower rate was in 2002.

faqs.q: Does Gordon County charge extra for card payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Credit card transactions carry a 2.50 percent convenience fee, charged by the processor. A mailed check avoids it.

faqs.q: Who can tell a closing attorney the real balance on a Gordon County parcel?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner's office, at 706-629-9242. A parcel may be under appeal without the website showing it, so call before closing.

faqs.q: By when must a Gordon County homeowner file for homestead exemption?
faqs.a: April 1 of the first year the owner wants it, and skipping the application is a waiver. In Gordon County the tax commissioner takes the applications.
